pageCache.pageTitle: Burntwood School - Our Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
At Burntwood, we believe that every student deserves an exceptional education, regardless of their starting point, interests or aspirations. Our ambition is to provide a rich, broad and balanced education that not only secures excellent academic outcomes, but also equips young people with the knowledge, skills and character to thrive in an ever-changing world.
Everything we do is underpinned by our commitment to developing confident, ambitious and compassionate young people. Through our curriculum, pastoral care and extensive programme of personal development, we encourage students to think critically, embrace challenge, discover new passions and grow into resilient individuals who are ready to lead, contribute and make a positive difference. At the heart of this is the Burntwood Way and our 5Cs: Character, Curriculum, Creativity, Community and Commitment. Together, they shape every aspect of school life and provide the foundation upon which our students develop into the women and men of tomorrow.
To provide a relevant and challenging education which enables all members of our community to reach their full potential.
To nurture creativity in students both in the classroom and beyond to help build cultural capital and instil an enjoyment of life long-learning.
To encourage students to be ambitious, bold and independent, with a strong sense of purpose and a commitment to their own academic and personal development.
To build a community in which everyone is respected and valued and where students have pride in their school and play a positive role in society.
To empower all students to exercise their inalienable rights as set out in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child.
Our philosophy is articulated through our long-standing motto: to provide the best education today for the women and men of tomorrow.

Principal's Welcome
It is my pleasure to welcome you to Burntwood School.
As we celebrate 40 years of educating girls, we remain as passionate as ever about our purpose: providing an exceptional education that enables every young woman to flourish academically, personally and socially. Our ambition is to ensure that every student leaves Burntwood with the confidence, knowledge, skills and character to shape their own future and make a meaningful contribution to the world around them.
For four decades, Burntwood has been recognised as a leader in girls’ education. We understand how girls learn, how they develop confidence and how to create an environment where they are challenged and nurtured to think critically, aim high and discover lifelong hobbies, skills and talents. Our students achieve excellent academic outcomes but, just as importantly, they leave us as articulate, resilient and ambitious young women, ready to embrace the opportunities and challenges that lie ahead.
Everything we do is guided by our 5Cs: Character, Curriculum, Creativity, Community and Commitment. These values shape every aspect of school life. Our broad and balanced curriculum is complemented by outstanding pastoral care, ensuring students feel supported and creating a learning environment where students are encouraged to be intellectually curious, creative into their thinking, and confident, articulate women. At the heart of Burntwood is a belief that every girl deserve to be known, valued and inspired to achieve her very best. Our excellent provision of enrichment, leadership, careers and co-curricular opportunities achieve this - helping our students broaden horizons, and develop and nurture lifelong interests and prepare them for life beyond school. Combined with our award-winning facilities, these experiences ensure that every student is able to make the very most of her time at Burntwood.
The greatest testament to our school is the young women who leave it. Every year we see students grow into confident individuals who are ready to contribute, lead and make a difference in their communities and beyond. It is a privilege to be part of that journey, and one that has defined Burntwood for the past 40 years.
I warmly invite you to visit us during one of our Open Events to experience Burntwood for yourself. Meet our students and staff, see learning in action and discover why generations of families have chosen Burntwood as the place where their daughters thrive.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to our Sixth Form
We are delighted to welcome you to Burntwood Sixth Form, a dynamic and aspirational community which ensures that all students achieve the very best personal and academic outcomes. At Burntwood Sixth Form, we value commitment, character, creativity and community – and aim to develop these through our rich curriculum. Our broad curriculum offers students the very best academic, vocational and technical qualifications, delivered by dedicated and passionate subject specialists. With over 30 A Levels, as well as BTEC and T Level courses to choose from, students at Burntwood are empowered to make the right choices to prepare them for their future successes. To complement our demanding and high-quality academic and pastoral curriculum, Burntwood Sixth Form offers a full range of exceptional enrichment and super-curricular opportunities, enabling all students to participate in a wide, rich and inspirational programme of study; this exceptional provision builds cultural capital and equips students with the skills and experiences to actively contribute to society. We are motivated by our longstanding and deeply-rooted commitment to provide all students with the best education today, empowering the citizens of tomorrow.

Provide a stable careers programme;
Educate students on labour market information;

Link curriculum learning to careers;
Provide multiple encounters with employers and employees;
Provide experience of the workplace;

Careers Guidance
We acknowledge the importance of impartial careers advice for all year groups, and career guidance is available to all students from our careers industry qualified adviser. In particular, one-on-one interviews are set up for each Year 11 student and actively encouraged for all Year 12 students.
Careers, Education and Work Related Learning
Careers education is incorporated into the school timetable, with each year group benefiting from dedicated careers related lessons. These are further supported by activities related to individual subject departments.
Careers education begins in Year 7 when students prepare to welcome and question an external visitor regarding their career and the choices they have made. This year's visitors included a lawyer, speech therapist, film producer, event manager, civil servant, community relations executive from a football foundation and the Metropolitan Police.
In Year 8, all students do reception duty for a day to have the opportunity to develop their work-related skills supporting staff and interacting with visitors to the school.
All Year 9 students are introduced to the Unifrog online careers programme where they explore their skills, and identify potential careers and the pathways to achieve them. An annual Careers Event provides Year 9 students with the chance to make contact with and explore a wide range of careers and occupations showcased by around 40 employers.
Year 10 students participate in a nationwide enterprise programme to learn technical and business disciplines as well as developing core enterprise and transferable skills. Burntwood also continues to offer a two-week work experience towards the end of the Summer Term. The opportunity introduces students to the world of work, gives them contact with real employers and help them develop their transferable skills. This experience is supported by full day preparation sessions when students consider employability skills, CV writing, interview skills, job applications and health and safety matters. After the work experience, students work through evaluating activities to reflect and record their learning experience.
Year 11 students take part in writing a progress file to help them chose sixth form courses, training or apprenticeships and meet one-on-one with the careers adviser to discuss their 16+ options.
The school encourages visits from organisations to introduce students to a wide range of career choices and industries including Science, Technology, Engineering and Maths (STEM), identified by the government as a priority.
Throughout the Sixth form years, a very extensive programme of careers and work-related activities is organised. Over 50 speakers and external facilitators visit the school and students are escorted on trips to employers. Specific student interests and pathways are identified early in the academic year and tailored opportunities and support is provided for pathways including Oxbridge, Medicine, Art and Design, Law, Nursing, IT and Business. External speakers including alumni, inform on the range of career pathways including school leaver and graduate apprenticeships. Year 12 students are encouraged and supported to set up work experience both within the enrichment period of the school week or following on from internal examinations.
Tutors provide support around the UCAS application and following on from internal examinations, Year 12 students attend workshops to register them on the UCAS process and support them as they draft their personal statement. Year 12 students attend university open days.
More information is provided on the Sixth Form Careers, WRL And UCAS page of the website.
(Note to Employers and WRL organisations: If you are able to offer WRL opportunities to Burntwood students, please email eking@burntwoodschool.com or sclarke@burntwoodschool.com)
Careers Information
Further and higher education resources are available in the sixth form study room and additional careers resources are available for all students in the library and the careers office.
In addition, careers opportunities relating to work experience, apprenticeships, courses and regularly updated labour market intelligence and opportunities are published on the school website and in a half term newsletter.

Provider Access Policy
For information on any of the information above, please contact Careers Link, Nick Bull on nbull@burntwoodschool.com, Lizzie King Sixth Form and Year 11 Careers and Stephen Clarke Year 7,8,9 and 10 Careers.

Student Leadership
At Burntwood School, we take every opportunity to provide our students with experiences that will equip them with the skills and knowledge to flourish in further education and beyond. In order for students to develop the confidence, experience and skill to become the women of tomorrow, opportunities for leadership are essential.
Students at Burntwood can participate in the Student Council, or be a Tutor Representative, in every year group. Additionally, in both the lower school and the Sixth Form we have Student Leadership Teams who meet regularly, discuss current issues and liaise with key members of staff. The Student Leadership Teams are voted democratically and are empowered to take decisions in the best interests of the entire student body. In the Sixth Form, our Head Students play a key role in representing the study body at key events. Furthermore, students in the lower school can develop their leadership skills through the Sports Leaders programme.

Special Educational Needs (SEND) Information Report
At Burntwood School, we are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive learning environment for all our students, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). We work closely with Wandsworth guidance to ensure that children with different additional needs are effectively supported within our mainstream setting. Our dedicated Learning Support team offers a range of interventions, including in-class support, individual programmes, and small group workshops focused on reading, writing, spelling, communication, and understanding

pageCache.pageTitle: Burntwood School - Sixth Form Careers & UCAS Support
pageCache.text:
Sixth Form Careers & UCAS Support
An independent Careers Adviser is available throughout the year to meet with students one on one and provide advice and guidance on all areas related to careers and Higher Education.
Throughout the year, weekly PSHE sessions, tutor periods and one on one careers meetings provide support to students with their career exploration and university and apprenticeship applications. In Autumn of Year 12 students focus on exploring their subject interests and awareness of careers, as well as developing their employability skills. A year assembly introduces the students to the importance of being proactive in maximising the huge number of opportunities and third parties such as the Early Careers Foundation are invited to provide employer mentoring . In Spring, they are introduced to Unifrog, a platform that helps students with the entire progression process - from exploring their interests, to recording all that they have done in Year 12, finding education, training and apprenticeship opportunities, to drafting their applications.
An Introduction to UnifrogStudents are encouraged to visit their university choices in June and September. They are finally led through the process of registering and completing a first draft of their personal statement for finalisation in Year 13 Autumn Term and / or applying for gap year experiences or apprenticeships.Special interest groups - Students with identified interests or strengths are guided through various application preparations such as for Medicine, Dentistry, Oxbridge, Law as well as for School Leaver Programmes. Students who articulate particular interests are targeted with specific opportunities. Oxbridge students are notified of Autumn and Spring Oxbridge taster days, invited to a school talk from an Oxbridge representative and supported in their interview preparation. Potential Russell Group candidates are invited to a motivational talk given by a Russell Group university. Law students are invited to visit legal firms, informed of taster days, university open days, London undergraduate mentoring programmes and work experience opportunities. Medical and Nursing students are supported with medical work experiences programmes at local hospitals, voluntary experience opportunities, specialist speakers on personal statement writing and interviews. Art, Drama and Dance Students are assisted through their particular application process. Similar opportunities exist for other industries including Computer Science, Business and Media.
Newsletter - Our regular online opportunity updates on Microsoft Teams alert students to a regular flow of ideas and opportunities for enrichment and career exploration for Year 12 and 13. Students can find insight events, workshops, higher apprenticeships and school leaver programmes, summer schools, work experience, post 18 and Higher Education, university insight and taster days and parent information.
We have an extensive programme of weekly speakers who visit the school to talk to students about their various career paths. Students are encouraged to request speakers if they have particular interests. These talks and careers activities are supported with professionally researched information sheets on different career and course pathways.
Students are also encouraged and supported to find work placements and voluntary opportunities as well as prepared for university or school leaver programme interviews with specialists e.g. science teachers for medicine, or other subject teachers and careers adviser for others.
Throughout the year, students are invited to attend school trips relating to careers. Annual examples include top Canary Wharf solicitors to hear about law, an award-winning architectural firm to find out about architecture and a top advertising agencies to hear about careers in marketing, media, advertising and communications.

Wellbeing
At Burntwood School we understand the importance of student wellbeing. We recognise that student’s emotional and physical wellbeing are essential components that lay a foundation to support students to achieve and thrive in education and beyond.
Our aim is to create an environment where students:
Feel safe, happy, and supported.
Our approach
Our approach is in-line with the The Department for Education (DfE) and the Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (2021) guidance which recommends the following eight principles:
We understand that good mental health and wellbeing helps students:
Our wellbeing offer is built on two interconnected areas:
attend school;
engage in learning;
achieve academically;
Pastoral Care
Our dedicated pastoral teams provide targeted support for students at every stage of their secondary school journey. From our form tutors who know each student as an individual, to our year teams who coordinate support across the year group, we ensure that every student has trusted adults they can turn to. We work closely with families and external agencies to provide early intervention and ongoing support when students face challenges.
Curriculum
We aim to give students the information they need to make good decisions about their own health and wellbeing, enabling them to recognise what is normal and what is an issue in themselves and others, and when issues arise, know how to seek support as early as possible from appropriate sources. Through our PSHE programme, Relationships and Sex Education, and Health Education, registration activities as well as through subjects across the curriculum, we equip students with the knowledge and skills to maintain positive mental and physical health.
Our provision

Attendance & Punctuality
Students need to attend school every day. There is a very clear link between attendance at school and academic achievements, therefore, the school is committed to ensuring that students attend every day.
A wide variety of research shows that attendance to school is directly linked to:
The expectation for all Burntwood Students is 97% attendance across the school year. A student with 6 days off school per year will not achieve this.
If there is a medical issue preventing them from attending, parents/carers must report the absence via the Expressions app before 8am on each day that they are absent
If your child is absent, and we do not receive a message as to why they are absent, you will be sent a truancy call at some stage during the morning. It is imperative that you respond to this, otherwise your child’s absence will be unauthorised. The decision to authorise an absence is entirely at the school’s discretion.
Burntwood School has an Attendance Team who will contact parents and carers if need be, and who works with families where there are concerns about attendance. Where a student’s attendance drops below 90% we will class the student as Persistently Absence/At risk of Persistent Absence, we may seek assistance from other outside agencies such as the Early Help Team within Social Services.

We also remind families that holidays should be taken in school holiday time, and that the school does not authorise Leave of Absence. Only emergencies or exceptional circumstances will be considered following consideration by the School Principal. Supporting documentation may be required.
A Fixed Penalty Notice (FPN) of £160 will be issued by the LEA, per parent, per child, for any unauthorised leave. If the FPN remains unpaid after 28 days you may be prosecuted for your child’s absence from school. Catering & Nutrition
Burntwood's catering service is provided by Pabulum, who provide healthy meals for our students, contributing to the School's Healthy School status.
The Pabulum team are delighted to provide the catering services at Burntwood School.
At Pabulum we are a devoted and dedicated team of food loving professionals with a passion for creating healthy, nutritionally balanced, delicious school meals. Our vision is to change the established eating order by bringing our passion, incredible ingredients, inspiring chefs, fresh food and smiling faces to hungry stude­nts.
Pabulum’s vision is to be at the forefront of improving the next generation’s health and well-being, by shaping the food culture in education that inspires a passion and love of fresh food. We value healthy, nutritious food provided by ethical suppliers, and we use 75% of British and seasonal produce in our menus. All of our meat and dairy produce is Red Tractor Assured.
We choose our supply partners based on their commitment to sustainability and have removed 70% virgin plastics from our range of disposables.
The fantastic industry leading Enjoy lunchtime offer features inspired destination dishes from around the globe and will naturally include delicious vegetarian and vegan choices. All Pabulum dishes are made fresh every day using seasonal, high-quality ingredients.
As well as the Enjoy destination dishes, students can choose from a range of hot and cold Grab ‘n’ Go items from the Enjoy Deli. Deli items include colourful salads, a wide range of wraps, filled baguettes and bloomer bread sandwiches accompanied by fresh fruit and homemade bakes.
Our 6th Form café is proudly serving Costa coffee. We’re open all day, because we know everyone is on a busy schedule. Pabulum’s amazing cafe food range mirrors the popular vibes of the high street. As well as healthy wraps, sandwiches and hot and cold deli, we offer an extensive range of Costa coffees and hot drinks, plus cakes and scones – fresh from the oven.

GCSE Examination Results 2025
Congratulations to all our Year 11s who collected their GCSE results in August 2025. Their hard work, determination and commitment led to some fabulous results; 25% of all our students’ results were grade 7 and above. They have achieved a fantastic set of results for Burntwood School; we are incredibly proud of all their achievements. This is despite the setbacks they had over the past few years. We welcome back all our students returning to our Sixth form, it is lovely to see so many of you back at Burntwood this term along with students who have chosen to join us from other schools.
